semantic_negative_mutation: Populate the context for exported page P with a label whose extracted_label_pages entry names a different page Q.
mechanical_invariant: Map iteration order, context container type, and local ID spelling are mechanical.
witness: Export P with an internal edge to that foreign label and observe a local target node or preserved local fragment for it.
refuted_by: Demonstrate that the foreign entry is absent from P's effective context and cannot resolve any P-local href.

semantic_negative_mutation: Omit a same-page label that has both a page entry for P and a homologous finite position.
mechanical_invariant: Ordering of context entries and target nodes is mechanical when the same graph and positions result.
witness: Export P with an edge to the omitted label and observe that no unique target node can close the edge despite complete registry data.
refuted_by: Show exactly one target at the measured position and a uniquely resolved owner edge to it.

semantic_negative_mutation: Pair a label's page entry with another label's position by independent filtering, sorting, or positional zip after an omission.
mechanical_invariant: Internal map representation and traversal strategy are mechanical; label-to-page-to-position association is semantic.
witness: Use labels A and B with distinct positions and one deliberately absent position; observe A or B targeted at the other's coordinates.
refuted_by: Resolve every included label to its own homologous recorded position and exclude only the entry whose own position is absent.

semantic_negative_mutation: Invent (0,0), the link location, or any fallback position for a same-page label whose extracted position is absent.
mechanical_invariant: Choice of diagnostic spelling and omission strategy is mechanical if no false node or preserved edge is produced.
witness: Provide a same-page label page entry without a homologous position and observe an emitted target node or a preservation claim.
refuted_by: Show that the label is excluded, its children remain visible, and no local fragment edge is emitted as preserved.

semantic_negative_mutation: Emit an internal href for a present label but omit its target node, misspell the referenced identity, or emit a node that cannot be resolved locally.
mechanical_invariant: Use of href versus xlink:href and concrete fragment token are mechanical when local resolution is equivalent.
witness: Parse the page-local semantic graph and find an internal link edge with zero matching target IDs.
refuted_by: Resolve the emitted edge to exactly one local node carrying the intended label identity.

semantic_negative_mutation: Emit two or more target nodes for one present label, or make one href resolve ambiguously through duplicate IDs.
mechanical_invariant: Target element kind and placement in serialization order are mechanical if one semantic node at the measured position results.
witness: Count graph nodes reached by the label's internal fragment and obtain more than one candidate or duplicate XML identities.
refuted_by: Show exactly one uniquely identifiable target node at the recorded position for the label.

semantic_negative_mutation: Assign the same local ID to two distinct labels or reuse an ID already owned by an unrelated SVG node.
mechanical_invariant: Prefix, hash algorithm, counter width, and ID text are mechanical; collision freedom in the emitted document is semantic.
witness: Use two distinct same-page labels plus an unrelated pre-existing ID and observe any owner edge resolving to the wrong or ambiguous node.
refuted_by: Show a one-to-one mapping from all destination labels to collision-free local identities and correct owner resolution.

semantic_negative_mutation: Derive identity from map iteration order, pointer/address, occurrence order, or unstable state so repeated equivalent exports change which label an edge reaches.
mechanical_invariant: Byte identity and literal ID stability are not required; bijective alpha-renaming and definition reordering are allowed.
witness: Repeat and reorder semantically equivalent registry input, normalize by bijective ID renaming, and observe a changed label-to-node graph, position, or edge ownership.
refuted_by: Show graph isomorphism preserving every label, position, owner edge, and unique resolution across repetitions and reorderings.

semantic_negative_mutation: For an internal edge whose label is absent from the page-local context, emit a fragment href, fabricate a node, remove the link's visual child, or claim preservation.
mechanical_invariant: Whether an inert wrapper remains and how Unknown is annotated are mechanical if visual children survive and no false resolved edge is claimed.
witness: Export a visible linked child with an absent label and observe a dangling/fabricated local edge, lost child, or Preserved classification.
refuted_by: Show visible children unchanged, no invented local target or fragment, and explicit Unknown/unsupported disposition.

semantic_negative_mutation: Convert a label belonging to another page into a same-page fragment or invent a filename/route in the standalone exporter without caller routing authority.
mechanical_invariant: Potential future route spelling is outside this owner; no spelling can legitimize an invented route.
witness: Export page P containing an edge to a label on Q with no explicit route and observe #id, guessed page URI, local node, or Preserved classification.
refuted_by: Show the edge remains Unknown with children visible and no dangling or invented href/node.

semantic_negative_mutation: Route LinkTarget::Url through destination context, rewrite/drop its scheme/query/fragment, or suppress it when the internal context is empty or colliding.
mechanical_invariant: Whether equivalent SVG consumers use href, xlink:href, or both is mechanical; the escaped URL value and link semantics must remain equivalent.
witness: Use an external URL containing query, fragment, ampersand, quotes, and non-ASCII characters; parse the SVG and observe a different resolved URL or missing external link.
refuted_by: Show the parsed anchor denotes the original external URL independently of destination-context contents.

semantic_negative_mutation: Insert a label-derived ID or fragment without XML/URI-safe encoding so reserved characters break the attribute, inject markup, or resolve to a different identity.
mechanical_invariant: The concrete escaping/encoding algorithm and resulting safe ID spelling are mechanical if edge and node share one unambiguous identity.
witness: Use labels containing ampersand, quotes, angle bracket, whitespace, percent, hash, and non-ASCII; observe malformed XML, injection, or href-to-id mismatch.
refuted_by: Parse successfully and resolve each adversarial label's owner edge to exactly one intended node with no injected structure.

semantic_negative_mutation: Flatten, discard, duplicate, or move visual descendants when wrapping a nested linked group, or reduce the clickable region to a different area.
mechanical_invariant: Choice of anchor wrapper nesting and transparent hit-shape encoding is mechanical if visual morphology and clickable region agree.
witness: Use a link around nested groups with multiple visible children and a known link box; compare morphology and hit region and observe missing/duplicated content or changed clickable area.
refuted_by: Show all descendants exactly once with unchanged morphology and the intended clickable region attached to the same link.

semantic_negative_mutation: Apply ancestor/group/link transform to the clickable area or internal destination node zero times, twice, or in a different basis from its visual content/recorded position.
mechanical_invariant: Transform may reside on equivalent wrappers or be composed algebraically; textual matrix form is mechanical.
witness: Use translated, rotated, and non-uniformly scaled nesting with a destination at a distinct measured point; observe displacement between visible content and hit area or between node and recorded position.
refuted_by: Show visual content, hit region, and destination node each occupy their required transformed positions with no relative drift.

semantic_negative_mutation: Call only a legacy empty-context SVG wrapper on the production compile-to-SVG path after deriving a nonempty page-local context, or fail to pass the context in the with-fonts branch.
mechanical_invariant: Helper names, allocation strategy, and whether context is borrowed or owned internally are mechanical within the approved immutable interface.
witness: Compile the same document through production SVG branches with and without resolved fonts and observe that a complete same-page destination registry fails to close an internal edge in either branch.
refuted_by: Show both explicit production branches receive the derived context and emit isomorphic closed destination graphs.

semantic_negative_mutation: Build the context from all document labels or from the wrong page index while the current pipeline exports only the selected first page.
mechanical_invariant: Page-index representation and traversal order are mechanical; selected-page membership is semantic.
witness: Use a two-page document with distinct same-named/independent labels and export the first page; observe a second-page node, position, collision, or route in the standalone first-page SVG.
refuted_by: Show the effective context contains only labels whose recorded page equals the actually exported page index.

semantic_negative_mutation: Change export_svg or export_svg_with_fonts so an absent explicit context implicitly discovers destinations, fabricates IDs, or alters existing unit-call output semantics.
mechanical_invariant: Incidental byte changes are not themselves a violation; the wrapper's empty-context semantic behavior is the invariant.
witness: Call each legacy wrapper on a Page containing an internal edge but no injected context and observe a claimed resolved local graph or invented destination state.
refuted_by: Show both wrappers behave as explicit empty-context calls: children preserved, internal destination unresolved/Unknown, external URLs unaffected.
